full_caption: Marbury Hollow Municipal Housing Authority, Appellant, v. Blackthorn Ridge Realty Trust, Appellee
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: Marbury Hollow Municipal Housing Authority, the association governing the Cinderfield subdivision, brought this action to enjoin Blackthorn Ridge Realty Trust from maintaining a detached structure at 3189 Harper's Cut, Lindenmere, CW in violation of Article III of the recorded declaration.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: Assessments levied under Article XII became a lien on the lot upon recording of the notice of assessment. The lien is subordinate to a first mortgage recorded earlier in time but superior to subsequent encumbrances.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: The defense of changed conditions requires a showing that the character of the neighborhood has so altered that the original purpose of the restriction can no longer be achieved. Isolated violations elsewhere in the subdivision do not meet that standard.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: A discretionary architectural approval power must be exercised reasonably and in good faith. A denial that states no articulable standard is arbitrary and will not support injunctive relief.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: The business judgment rule shields the board's maintenance and budgeting decisions from judicial second-guessing where the board acted within its authority, on an informed basis, and in the honest belief that the action served the association.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: Article III prohibits 'any outbuilding, shed or accessory structure exceeding one hundred twenty square feet.' The structure erected by Blackthorn Ridge Realty Trust measures 500 square feet and is therefore within the plain reach of the restriction.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: The association waived enforcement as to fence height by failing to act against 13 comparable violations over a period of 21 years. Selective enforcement of a covenant against one owner, after acquiescence in like violations by others, is inequitable.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: Covenants are construed in favor of the free use of land. Ambiguity in a restriction is resolved against the party seeking to enforce it, and a restriction will not be extended by implication to conduct not fairly within its terms.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: Fines totaling $250 were imposed without the hearing required by the bylaws. A fine imposed in disregard of the association's own procedural requirements is void, without regard to the merits of the underlying violation.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: The association's architectural review committee denied the application by letter dated July 28, 2024. The declaration requires that denials state the specific ground relied upon; the letter recited only that the proposal was 'not in harmony with the community.'

sections.heading: Paragraph 11
sections.text: Restrictive covenants are enforceable servitudes running with the land where they are (1) in writing, (2) intended to run, (3) touching and concerning the land, and (4) recorded so as to give notice to successors.

sections.heading: Paragraph 12
sections.text: We reverse the injunction as to the fence and affirm as to the accessory structure. The award of fines is vacated in its entirety.

sections.heading: RIDER 1 — ARCHITECTURAL REVIEW PROCEDURE
sections.text: No structure, addition, fence, or exterior alteration shall be commenced until plans have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Architectural Review Committee. The Committee shall act within 45 days of a complete submission; failure to act within that period constitutes approval. Any denial shall be in writing and shall identify the specific provision of the Declaration or published guideline on which it rests. Approval may not be withheld on grounds of personal taste alone.

sections.heading: RIDER 3 — ENFORCEMENT, FINES AND HEARING RIGHTS
sections.text: Before imposing any fine, the Board shall give the owner written notice of the alleged violation and an opportunity to be heard before the Board or a committee of at least three members who are not officers. Fines shall not exceed $250 per violation nor $5,000 in the aggregate for a continuing violation. A fine imposed without the notice and hearing required by this Rider is void.

sections.heading: RIDER 5 — MAINTENANCE ALLOCATION AND RESERVES
sections.text: The Association maintains the common areas, private drives and stormwater facilities. The owner maintains the Lot and all structures on it, including roofs, windows and exterior doors. The Board shall commission a reserve study not less often than every 21 years and shall fund reserves at not less than 75 percent of the study's recommended annual contribution.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Dispute Resolution
sections.text: Before filing suit, a party shall give written notice of the dispute and the parties shall confer in good faith for not fewer than 3 days, and shall thereafter submit the dispute to non-binding mediation before a mediator experienced in real property matters. This clause does not bar an action for injunctive relief to prevent irreparable harm or an action to preserve the status quo.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Time of the Essence
sections.text: Time is of the essence as to every obligation stated in this instrument. Where the final day for performance falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday in the State of Calloway, the period is extended to the next business day.

sections.heading: Clause 3 — Counterparts and Electronic Signature
sections.text: This instrument may be executed in counterparts, each of which is an original and all of which together constitute one instrument. A signature delivered electronically has the same effect as an original, provided that any instrument submitted for recording shall bear original signatures and acknowledgment before a notary public of the State of Calloway.
